children: The Bank of Korea is expected to raise its base rate by 25 bps to 3.25% at its policy meeting Thursday. Of 25 analysts surveyed by The Wall Street Journal, 23 expect a quarter-percentage-point rate increase in November after the BOK held steady in October. Some expect the BOK to revise up its growth and inflation forecasts for 2026 and 2027, as demand for chips used in artificial intelligence boosts exports and price pressure persist. Inflation remains above the 2% target, with both headline and core consumer prices rising 2.8% on year in October, while robust semiconductor exports continue to underpin growth, ING economists Deepali Bhargava and Lynn Song say in a note.(kwanwoo.jun@wsj.com)
